question.problem: The inverse of the function $f(x)={log}_{7}⁡(x+4)$ is ${f}^{-1}(x)=${{field-1}}.
question.worked_solution:
To find ${f}^{-1}(x),$ we start by replacing $f(x)$ with $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}y & ={log}_{7}⁡(x+4)\end{aligned}
$$

Now, interchanging $x$ and $y$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}x & ={log}_{7}⁡(y+4).\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we make $y$ the subject of the equation, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & ={log}_{7}⁡(y+4) \\ {7}^{x} & ={7}^{{log}_{7}⁡(y+4)} \\ {7}^{x} & =y+4 \\ y & ={7}^{x}-4\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the inverse function is ${f}^{-1}(x)={7}^{x}-4.$
